title: Week 5 Assessment: Careers, Money, Negotiation and Presenting
intro: This assessment checks how you plan a career, handle money decisions, negotiate and present. Part A is auto-graded from completed lessons. Part B has a decision scenario, a negotiation role-play and a written task. Answer as you would on the job.

items.prompt: You receive your first stipend of Rs 20,000. You have no savings and a Rs 4,000 monthly phone instalment. What is the most sensible first move?

options.text: Spend most of it on gadgets.
Make a simple budget, set aside a small emergency fund first and track spending for the month.
options.feedback: A budget and emergency fund are basic foundations.

options.text: Lend all of it to a friend.
options.feedback: Large loans without planning are risky.

options.text: Put it all into one risky investment.
options.feedback: Putting everything in a risk is unwise.

items.why: Build a budget and a small buffer before taking risks.

items.setup: You receive a job offer from an IT services firm. The salary is slightly below the range you researched for entry-level roles, and you want to negotiate respectfully.

turns.they: We are happy to offer you the role at this salary. Please confirm.

options.text: I will take it, no questions.
options.feedback: Accepting without discussion forfeits your chance.

options.text: Thank you, I am excited about the role. Based on my research for similar entry-level roles, could we discuss a figure closer to the middle of that range?
options.feedback: Appreciation, evidence and a clear request.
options.reply: Let me see what is possible.

options.text: This is too low. Give me more.

turns.they: The budget is limited. What would make this work for you?

options.text: I would value a slightly higher base, or a joining bonus and a review after six months. Which is easier for you?
options.feedback: Offers flexible options with a trade-off.
options.reply: We can look at a six-month review.

turns.they: We can do a six-month review with a revised figure. Does that work?

options.text: Yes, please put it in writing.
options.feedback: Confirming and requesting it in writing protects you.
options.reply: Of course, we will email it.

options.feedback: A weak reply risks later misunderstanding.
Walking away without trying options wastes the progress.

items.why: Prepare evidence, ask for a specific outcome, explore options and confirm in writing.

items.prompt: You have five minutes to present your learning project to a panel. Write 100 to 130 words describing your core message, a three-part structure with time split and how you will handle one tough question.
items.modelAnswer: Message: A daily practice routine can make a beginner ready for ABAP tasks in eight weeks. Structure: one minute opening with a hook about interview rejections, three minutes with three points (habit, practice problems, review of errors) and one minute close with a call to join the group. If asked why not another language, I will acknowledge the question, explain that the target role uses ABAP, answer briefly and ask if that addresses their concern.
items.guidance: Strong answers give one claim with a reason, a clear three-part time split and a calm structured response to a question. Avoid listing many messages.
